title: Predictive surge coordinator and grace invoice allocator
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a Predictive Surge Coordinator (PSC) that combines short-window traffic forecasting with conservative soft-crediting and an automated invoice smoothing allocator for temporary burst usage. Goal: provide predictable performance during transient spikes while reducing surprise overage charges for customers and lowering operator toil for manual corrections.
background: Customers on Dedicated fleets experience occasional short high-QPS spikes from periodic jobs and traffic storms. Current surge pools provide capacity but billing for these transient bursts results in many invoice disputes and manual refunds. We need a coordinated system that: (a) forecasts imminent surge risk, (b) proactively assigns temporary soft credits or short-lived surge lanes, (c) applies meter-level attribution rules, and (d) runs a deterministic retrospective smoothing job that reconciles soft credits with actual sustained usage for billing clarity.
goals: Integrate a short-horizon traffic predictor into fleet admission to identify likely 1-15 minute spikes
Provide configurable soft-credit windows (default 10 minutes) that automatically allocate surge capacity without immediate invoice overage
Create a deterministic retrospective smoothing pipeline that recalculates prorated charges and issues customer-facing invoice adjustments within 24 hours
Expose operator and tenant visibility in Console for active surge allocations and pending invoice adjustments
Keep tail latency SLOs during spikes via fast-path admission and graceful throttling if capacity unavailable
non_goals: Replace long-term reserved capacity or formal committed burst products
Handle multi-day sustained overage billing reconciliations (outside 24h smoothing window)
Full ML re-training infra for prediction models (initial rollout uses lightweight heuristic + LR model)
design_decisions: Use a hybrid predictor: recent token request rate + gradient features with an exponential smoothing baseline. Not a heavy neural model to keep inference cheap and explainable
Soft credits are ephemeral tokens scoped to tenant+route and expire after the configured window. They are not a billing credit until reconciled by the smoothing job
Retrospective smoothing is deterministic and idempotent: same input data yields same invoice adjustments. Smoothing runs in a strict order to avoid double-posting credits
Default tenant policy: 10 minute soft window, 2x headroom multiplier. Enterprise tenants can configure via Dedicated Console
Operator controls: manual override to force grant/revoke surge lanes, and a read-only ledger of all grants and reconciliations
acceptance_criteria: PSC exposes an HTTP probe and telemetry: predicted_spike_prob, predicted_multiplier, decision_reason
Console shows active soft credits for tenant with start_time, expiry_time, estimated_capacity
Smoothing job produces a delta line-item per tenant for bursts within 24h and posts adjustment to billing queue; results reconciled in sandbox invoices during e2e tests
No regression in 99.9th percentile tail latency across canary fleets under synthetic spike tests
Integration tests covering edge cases: overlapping soft windows, multiple overlapping tenants, and predictor false-positive/negative scenarios
work_items: PSC: predictor service + admission hook implementation
Soft credit ledger: schema + compact immutable log + GC policy
Smoothing pipeline: reconciler job, idempotency guards, billing integration
Console UI: surge timeline, ledger view, manual override buttons
Operator runbook: playbook for audit, rollback, and dispute handling
End-to-end test harness: synthetic traffic generator and invoice validation
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Predictor false negatives cause missed capacity => mitigate by conservative multiplier and immediate fallback to existing surge pools
Risk: Incorrect smoothing yields billing disputes => mitigate with canary stage publishing adjustments to sandbox invoices and human-in-the-loop approval for first 48h
Risk: Increased operator confusion => provide clear Console UX and training docs, + telemetry events explaining decisions
Risk: Abuse by tenants gaming soft credits => limit per-tenant soft credit frequency and add heuristics for repetitive short spikes
deployment_plan: Phase 1: implementation and internal canary on test fleets (2 weeks)
Phase 2: closed beta with 3 enterprise tenants, soft credits only (2 weeks)
Phase 3: broad rollout with smoothing enabled but first-48h manual approval for adjustments (2 weeks)
Phase 4: automation of smoothing and full release once metrics stable (ongoing)
qa_plan: Unit tests for predictor and ledger logic
Integration tests that simulate bursts at 1m, 5m, 10m windows
Billing e2e that verifies adjustment lines in sandbox invoices
Chaos test: random revoke/grant sequence to verify idempotency
